product.intro: Set up one month with a salary, a few expenses, and the bills still due. Then use the same routine each month. All examples below use fictional records.

sections.title: Try one month in the demo
paragraphs: Open the sample household and read the Home card. This household recorded ₹84,000 in income and ₹12,740 in expenses. It still has ₹25,700 in bills due, leaving an estimated ₹45,560.
Home calculates Left after bills from the income and expenses logged for the selected month, minus bills still due. The figure changes as you log records. Savings are shown separately.
figure: Monthly Home showing income, expenses, bills due and ₹45,560 left after bills
In this sample month, ₹84,000 − ₹12,740 − ₹25,700 = ₹45,560. Use the arrows beside the month to review earlier periods.

sections.title: Record a salary or other income
paragraphs: The demo lets you explore. Sign in to enter records for your own household.
steps: On Home, choose Add income.
Enter a name such as Salary, the amount received, and the date it arrived.
Choose Save income. Check Income received on Home. Expand Income this month to review or edit an entry.
sections.note: Use the date you received the money. Use the month selector if you want to check a previous month after saving.

sections.title: Log and find an expense
paragraphs: Start with the amount and category. Add details when they help you recognise or find the purchase later.
steps: Choose Add expense. Enter an amount such as ₹450 and pick a category.
Check the date. Add a description such as Saturday groceries. Add a person, platform, or receipt when useful.
Save the expense. Open Expenses, check the date range and search for Saturday groceries to find the entry or open it for editing.
figure: Expense ledger with a date range, search, and sample transaction rows
Check the period first when an expense you expect is missing.

sections.title: Pay a bill without counting it twice
steps: On Home, choose Manage bills, then Add bill. Enter its name, expected amount, due date, and how often it repeats. Choose Save bill.
Find the due bill and choose Record payment.
If the amount is already in Expenses, choose Already logged it?, select the matching entry, and choose Link expense. If it is a new payment, confirm the amount and date and choose Save payment.
Expand Paid to find the payment. The linked expense stays in the ledger and the bill stops counting as due.
figure: Bills and EMIs view separating upcoming and paid sample bills
Marking a bill paid moves its occurrence to Paid. Link the existing ledger entry if you already recorded the payment.
sections.note: A repeated rent or EMI gets a new occurrence for its next due period. Linking applies to the occurrence you’re paying.

sections.title: Review spending before changing a budget
steps: Open More → Budgets to set a monthly amount for a category.
Open More → Overview and select the month. Compare actual spending with your plan and check the category breakdown.
If a total looks high, open Expenses and review the entries for that period before changing the budget.

sections.title: Record a savings balance
paragraphs: Use Savings for amounts you’ve already set aside, such as an emergency fund or fixed deposit.
steps: Open Savings and choose Add savings or investment.
Enter the name, type, latest value and the date you checked it. Choose Save value.
When you check it again, open the same holding and use Update value.
figure: Savings view with three holdings and the date for each recorded amount
The date beside a holding tells you when that balance was entered.
sections.note: FinBuddy shows recorded values. Keep cash-flow entries in Income and Expenses, and balances in Savings.

sections.title: When something looks wrong
table: Verify the signed-in account and date range, then clear the search or category filters.
Open Manage bills and check the occurrence for that month. Open Paid to see recorded payments.
Check Income received, Expenses logged, and Bills still due for the same month.
Open Savings and check the as-of date for the holding. Use Update value after checking the balance.
Use the provider you signed up with. For an email password, choose Forgot password? on sign-in.
links: Change your appearance or manage API access
Report a problem without sharing your records

settings.intro: Open More → Settings in the signed-in workspace. Preferences controls how this device looks. Developer Options manages tokens for this account.

sections.title: Choose how FinBuddy looks
paragraphs: Settings opens to Preferences. Choose the display mode, palette, and font individually.
table: Choose Light, Dark, or System. System follows your device.
Choose a palette, including Black & white. This controls colours, and works with your chosen display mode.
Choose Source Sans 3, Source Code Pro, Lato, Open Sans, Ubuntu, Source Serif 4, Lora, or Roboto.
sections.note: Changes apply to the current browser and device. Choose Reset appearance to restore all three defaults.

sections.title: Create a token for one integration
steps: In Settings, choose Developer Options in the Settings sidebar.
Give the token a name you’ll recognise, such as Monthly export. Select read-only for reports or read/write when the integration needs to change records.
Choose an expiration. The default is 30 days. Other choices are 7 days, 90 days, and Never expires.
Generate the token and complete recent sign-in if prompted. Copy the displayed token before leaving Developer Options.
sections.note: The token accesses the FinBuddy account that created it. Store it in your integration’s secret store and keep it out of screenshots, source code, and support requests.

sections.title: Test and revoke a token
steps: Open Swagger, choose Authorize, and paste your token.
Try GET /profile as a small read-only check and look for a 200 response.
When you stop using the integration, return to Developer Options and revoke the named token.
links: Run the same check from a terminal

technical.intro: Run the workspace with sample data, trace where records go, and make your first read-only API request.

sections.title: Run the demo locally
paragraphs: Install Git, Node.js 24 and Python 3.12. Run these commands in a terminal. The FinBuddy handbook is generated before Vite starts.
sections.code:
git clone https://github.com/theharithsa/finbuddy.git
cd finbuddy
npm ci
npm run dev
sections.note: Open the local URL printed by Vite and add ?demo=1. Open /docs/ on the same server to see the Help Center. The sample household is the quickest path when you’re inspecting the UI.

sections.title: Trace a record from the screen to storage
paragraphs: The React and TypeScript workspace runs in the browser. Firebase Authentication supplies the signed-in identity. Firestore rules and Storage rules govern browser access, and the REST API checks token scope and record ownership before serving account data.
table: Enter an expense in the app
src/features/expenses/ → Firebase client → account records in Firestore.
Attach a receipt in the app
Expense editor → Cloud Storage for the file → expense metadata in Firestore.
Read an expense through the API
Firebase Hosting /api/v1 → Firebase Functions in api/ → Firestore. The API checks the personal token and account scope.
src/features/workspace/DemoWorkspace.tsx → fictional data. No account is needed.

sections.title: Make your first API request
paragraphs: Use Swagger first, or copy the Bash example below (Git Bash also works on Windows). It prompts for the token privately and clears the variable afterward.
steps: Create a read-only token in More → Settings → Developer Options.
In Swagger, choose Authorize, then GET /profile → Try it out → Execute.
Look for 200 and your profile. A 401 means the request needs a valid token. A 403 on a write request means the token lacks write scope.
sections.code:
read -rs -p "FinBuddy read-only token: " FINBUDDY_TOKEN
printf "\n"
curl --fail-with-body --silent --show-error \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FINBUDDY_TOKEN" \
  https://finbuddy-2025.web.app/api/v1/profile
unset FINBUDDY_TOKEN

sections.title: Handle money and retries correctly
table: Amounts are decimal INR with up to two fractional digits.
Read income, bills, holdings or monthly summary
Amounts use integer paise. ₹450 is 45000 paise.
The remaining amount is income minus recorded expenses. Home’s Left after bills also subtracts unpaid bills.
Use limit and follow the opaque nextCursor until the response omits it.
Send an Idempotency-Key and reuse it for retries of the same body. A conflicting body returns 409. Bill payments deduplicate by occurrence.
links: Read the API contract and examples

sections.title: Test writes against emulators
paragraphs: Use Java 21. Run the web browser suite from the repository root with Node.js 24.
sections.code:
npx --no-install playwright install chromium
npx --yes firebase-tools@14.20.0 emulators:exec --only auth,firestore,storage --project demo-finbuddy "npm run test:browser"
sections.note: For the API suite, use Node.js 22, install the API’s locked dependencies with npm --prefix api ci, and use the isolated API configuration in the testing guide. Both suites use fictional accounts and the demo-finbuddy project.

sections.title: Preview a handbook change
paragraphs: Update the guide source when a change affects what a visitor sees. Use an empty output directory for Pages.
sections.code:
python scripts/build_public_docs.py --output dist/public-docs
python -m http.server 8080 --directory dist/public-docs

sdlc.intro: FinBuddy ships through a checked pull request to main. This guide shows how to take one product change from issue to live verification.

sections.title: Give the issue a testable outcome
paragraphs: Example: On a phone, a visitor looking for help can find the bill-payment steps from the Help Center.
steps: Create or reuse an issue and set the type, owner and milestone. Check that it appears on the FinBuddy GitHub Project.
Write the user outcome and how you’ll verify it. For data or account changes, include the access and recovery cases.
Order work from its dependencies. Use a Sprint field when work is scheduled.

sections.title: Open a reviewable PR
steps: Branch from main, keep the change focused, and link the issue with Closes #N for completed work or Refs #N for part of the work.
Update any affected guide in the same PR. Under Documentation impact, write Updated: followed by the affected guides, or No change: followed by the reason.
Record what you ran, what you saw at phone and desktop sizes if relevant, and how to recover the affected release.
sections.code:
## Documentation impact

Updated: Product handbook — added the steps for linking an existing expense to a bill payment.

sections.title: Check the actual candidate
paragraphs: Use the current diff and resolve review threads. Main requires foundation, verify and verify-api on a candidate that is up to date. The repository uses a solo-maintainer policy with zero independent approvals.
table: Exercise the before and after path with sample or emulator data. Check keyboard and phone widths for UI changes.
Exercise owner, wrong-account and signed-out cases when relevant. Verify old records and the recovery plan.
Open the actual changed pages from the landing page and Help Center. Walk through the instructions and test links.
Review affected callers and compatibility. Add the documentation decision to the bot-authored PR.

sections.title: Verify what users received
steps: Follow the CI/CD pipeline from the merged SHA to Hosting verification and Pages publication.
Open both public URLs and test the changed path. Record the completed workflow, live revision, and any failures or recovery in the issue.
Use the release procedure to restore the affected surface if it needs recovery.

pipeline.intro: The pull request proves the change. Main builds the release artifact, verifies the deployed app, and then publishes the product site for the same revision.
stages: Foundation checks repo contracts, docs and links. Web and API jobs test real user and account paths with Firebase emulators.
Re-run web and API checks. Upload the production web bundle and the generated Help Center as the finbuddy-hosting artifact.
Deploy that artifact. Check the live Git SHA, cached asset rules, icons and API routes before continuing.
Build the product site and handbook from the same Git revision. Publish after Hosting verification passes.

sections.title: Read the check that failed
table: The PR documentation decision, repository contracts, and both public builds.
Lint, JavaScript tests, browser flows on Firebase emulators, or the Vite build.
API unit and contract tests, or the isolated emulator suite.
The Firebase Hosting deploy receipt, live revision verification, and API smoke results.
The Pages package, deploy result, and public handbook revision.

sections.title: Recover the affected surface
paragraphs: The automated Hosting check retries the same read-only check for a brief revision propagation delay. A persistent mismatch or a failing asset or API check stops Pages publication.
steps: Find the failed job and identify the revision it tested.
Verify which revision each host is serving before retrying. Keep failed checks visible in the issue.
Use the release procedure to recover only the affected service. Recheck the actual public path and record what users can now see.

roadmap.intro: Track which features you can use today and what needs to happen before FinVision can appear in FinBuddy. FinVision is in discovery and has no scheduled release date.
stages: Agree on account and data ownership
Current stage. Map how the two apps identify the same user and agree on which data FinBuddy can show.
After approval of the data boundary, pick the first view and specify how updates and conflicts are handled.
When the slice is ready, test identity, permissions, sync and recovery with fictional accounts before a limited pilot.
Decide on wider access after the pilot confirms the behaviour. Set a target window at that stage.

sections.title: In the workspace today
paragraphs: Households can record income and expenses, set category budgets, manage bill payments, and track dated savings values. The public demo lets you explore the month without an account.

sections.title: FinVision discovery
paragraphs: The first slice is intended for signed-in FinBuddy users. It will show only the agreed set of FinVision records. The project is currently deciding identity, ownership and sync. The discovery milestone has no due date.

sections.title: Other planned work
table: Use Home and Overview to review recorded income and spending.
Use Overview for monthly category and spending insights.
Backlog. Scope, permitted actions and availability are undecided.
The REST API supports direct integrations.

sections.title: What’s new on the website
paragraphs: The Help Center now walks through a first month, from adding income to matching a bill payment. Developers can run the demo locally and follow a read-only API example. Start with the guide that matches what you need.
